QF.id: Issue Management - General Obligations and Due Diligence_44

question.text: For a Fast Track Rights Issue, what is the minimum average market capitalization of public shareholding required?

explanation.text: The Logic: To be eligible for a Fast Track Rights Issue (FTRI), the average market capitalization of the company's public shareholding must be at least Rs. 250 crore. This is computed on at least one stock exchange with nationwide trading terminals over a defined look-back period preceding the reference date. The Trap: The Rs. 1,000 crore figure is the corresponding threshold for a Fast Track Public Issue (FTPI), not for a Fast Track Rights Issue — candidates who recall "fast track" generically and pick Rs. 1,000 crore confuse the two routes. Rs. 500 crore and Rs. 100 crore do not correspond to either route's published threshold. In the ambiguous original wording ("For a Fast Track Issue"), both Rs. 250 crore (rights) and Rs. 1,000 crore (public) could be defended. Note: The original stem said only "Fast Track Issue", which is ambiguous because the workbook (NISM-Series-IX Merchant Banking, p.100 and p.155) lists Rs. 250 crore for a fast-track rights issue and Rs. 1,000 crore for a fast-track public issue. The stem has been narrowed to "Fast Track Rights Issue" so the keyed Rs. 250 crore is now the unique correct answer.
